outcomes: Every Go workload answers the same operational paths, so one orchestrator configuration works across services
A dependency that reports its own health appears on the probe endpoints without extra wiring
A workload that declares a required dependency but never wires it up is reported unready rather than accepted
A slow or hung probe delays the answer by a bounded amount instead of holding the endpoint open
nonGoals: Authenticating the operational endpoints; they mount unauthenticated and are expected to sit on a trusted or prefixed surface
Defining what makes a dependency healthy, which each probe owns
Exporting metrics directly: the module takes no OpenTelemetry dependency and offers a callback seam instead
Promising strict compatibility between every pre-1.0 minor release

requirements.text: The plugin mounts liveness, health, readiness, and version paths under the configured prefix, and mounts profiling handlers only when the workload enables them explicitly.

A platform plugin added to an application mounts its endpoints on the application's single server when the application configures, in any plugin order, and mounts them once however often the application configures. An application that holds no server, or several, fails configure with an error that names RegisterOn. A plugin mounted through RegisterOn registers nothing more.
The liveness path runs no probes and consults no running flag, so it answers success whenever the process can serve a request and never causes a restart because a dependency is slow.
The health and readiness aggregates report unavailable before the application starts and after it stops, and report degraded with per-probe detail when any probe fails.

Probe discovery walks the module tree on the first aggregate request rather than during configure, so a probe contributed by a plugin configured later is still found, and an explicitly registered probe is never overwritten by a discovered one of the same name.

Probe names are validated against the cross-language probe-name pattern when registered explicitly, and a discovered or required name that violates it fails application start rather than emitting an envelope the protocol's own validator would reject.
Probes run in parallel, each under its own timeout, and the aggregate answers after a bounded grace period even when a probe ignores cancellation.
A readiness probe named as required but never registered or discovered makes readiness degraded with a synthesized failing entry, while health deliberately ignores the required list.
When error redaction is enabled a failing probe reports a generic message to the caller while the real cause is logged server-side, so unauthenticated endpoints do not disclose internal topology.
The version path returns the configured build metadata, and empty fields fall back to the binary's embedded build information rather than being reported as known-empty.
